rows: Reported on the south side of Highway 190.
Trees, power lines, and large tree limbs down around the city. A carport was also blown away. Most of the damage was reported on the south side of Highway 190.
Orange to grapefruit-size hail was reported along Highways 36 and 182. A greenhouse was destroyed and dozens of cars were damaged with windshields broken.
Trees down on CR 315 and power lines down on CR 318.
Dime-size hail gradually increased to baseball-size throughout the duration of the storm. Extensive damage occurred to churches in the area. Reported by cooperative observer.
A roof was blown off a building and trees were blown down.
USAF forecaster reported a tornado near KGRK radar. No damage reported.
Tornado formed in open country; no damage reported.
A barn was blown onto FM 929.

A damage survey conducted by the National Weather Service Forecast Office in Fort Worth revealed that a tornado developed just south of CR 315 and moved rapidly north-northeast. It damaged numerous trees along CR 315 and FM 107. As the tornado moved just west of Oglesby, it damag…
Golfball-size hail reported by military personnel.
Barns and two homes were damaged. Trees were also blown down.

A brief tornado which touched down in Lampasas County continued into Coryell County, damaging portions of Sleepy Hollow Lane and Carroll Drive. Several homes sustained minor damage. One home was blown slightly off its foundation, while others had damage to roofs and decks. Trees …
A tornado was reported south of Highway 84 and CR 177 and moved east before dissipating. Only tree damage was noted.
Golfball-size hail covered the ground on Highway 116.
Quarter-size hail was reported at the intersection of Highway 116 and FM 1783.

Roofs were ripped off two buildings in downtown Gatesville. At least ten utility poles and numerous large trees and tree limbs were blown down. Seven large windows had to be replaced on the Coryell County courthouse after they were shattered by debris from the storm. The Stillhou…
A report of half-dollar size hail was relayed by broadcast media.
Two 13' x 150' sheds holding chickens, geese, and quail were destroyed by an isolated downburst. Both structures rolled, killing or injuring some of the birds and releasing others.
Several trees along with a high school scoreboard were blown down. Several trees fell across roadways.
A 74 MPH wind gust was measured at the AWOS 3 miles west of Gatesville.

A gas station near the intersection of US HWY 84 and State HWY 36 had its windows blown in. A sheriff's deputy was injured in the eye by blowing glass. High winds damaged an overhead door at a fire station in Gatesville. A business next to the fire station had the roof blown off.…
Quarter size hail fell in Oglesby.
Nickel size hail covered the ground in the western portions of Copperas Cove.
Hail up to Tennis Ball size was covering the ground in Evant.
Penny size hail was reported at Fort Hood on the Coryell County side.
The metal roof of a barn on Luthern Church Road was blown off. A second barn in the same area was also damaged.
Multiple trees were blown down across county roads and a structure was pushed into County Road 321 near Leon Junction.
Hail the size of a thumb fell north of Topsey. The amount of hail was large enough to nearly cover the ground.

Significant damage occurred to a double wide home on CR 118 north of Topsey. Strong winds destroyed three sheds, one of which was a car shed. The winds also tore shingles off the roof and the side of the home. Some eaves of the home were also damaged, and a 2x4 was driven though …
Damage to two sheds occurred at the Topsey Exotic Ranch. The roof was blown off one shed and the tin bent up on another shed. A flagpole was also bent.
A 60 MPH wind gust was measured in Copperas Cove. A local newspaper reported some property damage was reported in Copperas Cove, but no other information was given.
A 67 MPH wind gust was measured just east of Copperas Cove.
The local newspaper reported a few trees were down in Ater and were blocking roads.
The local newspaper reported some trees down in Gatesville, but no other property damage was reported.
The local newspaper reported a few trees were down in Oglesby and were blocking roads.
The local newspaper reported a few trees were down in The Grove area and were blocking roads.
A brief tornado touched down at Mother Neff State Park near the cave. At least six trees were twisted and snapped. The trees were at least a foot in diameter.
Nickel size hail was reported by a CoCoRaHS observer south of Copperas Cove.
Dime size hail was reported between the cities of Gatesville and Levita.
Nickel to half dollar sized hail was reported in Copperas Cove.
Baseball sized hail fell in Evant.
Several homes suffered roof damage in downtown Evant due to high winds. The metal roof of the old firehouse was torn off and several large trees were also knocked down.
A brief tornado occurred approximately 6 miles east of Evant, just north of Highway 84. Some minor tree damage occurred.
Hail stones ranging from 2 to just over 3 in diameter fell in Topsey.
Tennis ball sized hail fell about 9 miles northeast of Copperas Cove.

The chimney of a home on Knowles Road near Ogelsby was knocked off the home by strong thunderstorm winds. A tractor and three cars on the property were also damaged. The carport at his neighbor's house was blown across the yard.
Numerous large tree limbs and some large trees were blown down near Fort Hood. Wind speeds were estimated to be around 60 mph.
Emergency management reported winds estimated at 50 to 60 MPH in Gatesville.
Photos of tree damage and tin roof damage were relayed from broadcast media via NWS chat.
Trained Spotters reported golf ball sized hail, nine miles east of Evant.
Trained spotters reported nickel to quarter sized hail, approximately 12 miles east of Evant.
Ping pong ball sized hail was reported 7 miles west of Gatesville.
Quarter sized hail was reported at the intersection of Highway 36 and 360.
Quarter to hen egg sized hail was reported in Evant over a ten minute period.
Penny sized hail was reported south of Evant between US 281 and FM 183.
Ping pong ball sized hail was reported on FM 1690.
Dime to quarter sized hail with heavy rain was reported in Evant.
The public reported 1 inch hail in Gatesville.
The public reported 1.5 inch hail near Gatesville.

A National Weather Service damage survey team found evidence of a nearly six mile tornado path across much of Coryell County and an extremely small part of Fort Hood. The tornado began near Farm to Market Road 580 where it crosses Table Rock Creek. From there, the tornado moved n…
Coryell County Sheriff's Department reported trees blown down near the town of Pearl, TX.
The sheriff's office reported trees had fallen on CR 274, blocking the road and requiring removal.
Broadcast media reported nickel-sized hail near the intersection of Hwy 84 and FM 1996.
Broadcast media reported nickel to dime sized hail covering the ground on FM 929.
A trained spotter reported quarter to half-dollar sized hail in Ireland, TX.
Spotters reported quarter to golf ball sized hail approximately one mile east-northeast of Copperas Cove. Damage was done to several vehicles.
A public report confirmed wind damage to an HEB Grocery Store sign and multiple street lights bent from thunderstorm winds in Gatesville, TX.
Homes in the Coryell City area were damaged due to thunderstorm winds.

A National Weather Service storm survey crew found evidence of damage consistent with EF-2 winds in Coryell County. Two homes were damaged to the point where most of their roof was removed. Several barns were destroyed as well, as were multiple pieces of farm and ranch equipment.
The Gatesville, TX AWOS recorded a thunderstorm wind gust of 58 MPH.
A trained spotter reported quarter-sized hail near the weather station at Fort Hood.
A broadcast media report indicated golf-ball sized hail in the city of Purmela, TX.
Broadcast media reported quarter-sized hail approximately 10 miles west-northwest of the city of Gatesville, TX.
A storm chaser reported trees down between the communities of Flat and The Grove.
Penny sized hail was reported at Fort Hood Military Base.
Fort Hood soldiers reported penny-sized hail near the intersection of Murphy Road and 53rd street.
A trained spotter reported nickel-sized hail on Highway 377 approximately 4 miles west-southwest of the city of Copperas Cove, TX.
Broadcast media reported nickel sized hail in the city of Jonesboro, TX.
Amateur radio reported quarter-sized hail approximately 9 miles east of the city of Evant, TX.
A trained spotter reported multiple trees down approximately 1 mile west of the city of Evant, TX along Hwy 84.
Broadcast media reported damage to the roofs of homes in the Copperas Cove area.
A trained spotter reported quarter size hail in the city of Jonesboro, TX.
A trained spotter reported a very brief tornado north of Levita but south of Jonesboro in Coryell County. The location is estimated based on radar.

A homeowner on Self Road between Pearl and Izoro reported damage to many trees on their property. In her words: One large live oak and two large elms were completely knocked down, many large limbs and the tops of many trees were ripped off, a massive cedar looked like the top was…

An isolated supercell thunderstorm produced an EF-2 tornado near the border separating extreme southern Coryell County from extreme eastern Lampasas County, Texas. Officials reported that approximately 196 residences in the City of Copperas Cove were impacted to varying degrees. …
A trained spotter reported quarter size hail near the city of Copperas Cove, TX.
A trained spotter reported quarter sized hail east southeast of Gatesville.
A trained spotter reported quarter sized hail east of Gatesville.
Hail ranging from nickel to ping pong ball size was reported on the west side of Copperas Cove.
A trained spotter reported ping pong ball size hail.

Four small aircraft were overturned at the Gatesville Airport and significant damage was reported to at least 1 hanger. Seven other hangers sustained damage. A handful of trees were also reported down the across the city of Gatesville.

A tornado was documented by pictures and videos over the Fort Hood military base. This area is undeveloped and has little access. No damage was reported. Times and path were determined by using visual reports and radar tracking of a tornadic debris signature.
A public report indicated half-dollar sized hail about 2 miles east-southeast of Copperas Cove, TX.
A public report indicated quarter sized hail about 3 miles northwest of Copperas Cove, TX.
Amateur radio reported ping pong ball sized hail about a mile south-southwest of Pidcoke.
A public report indicated 2-inch diameter hail in Gatesville, TX.
A public report indicated 2-inch diameter hail about 2 miles east-northeast of South Mountain, TX.
A public report indicated half-dollar sized hail about a mile north-northeast of Fort Gates, TX.
A public report indicated 2-inch diameter hail about 4 miles north-northwest of Oglesby, TX.
A public report indicated quarter sized hail about 8 miles southeast of Fort Gates, TX.
Amateur radio reported golf ball sized hail near Arnett, TX.
RFD winds were determined to be the cause of damage at a home on Longview Circle that lost part of its roof. The RFD winds could have been near 95 mph.
A trained spotter reported quarter sized hail about a mile south-southeast of Fort Gates, TX.
Fire and rescue reported quarter sized hail at the North Fort Hood Fire Station on the Longhorn and Shorthorn Airfields.
A trained spotter reported half-dollar sized hail 1 mile south-southeast of Gatesville, TX.
Amateur radio reported quarter sized hail 1 mile west-northwest of Copperas Cove, TX.
A public report indicated quarter sized hail 3 miles northwest of Copperas Cove, TX.
A public report indicated golf ball sized hail 8 miles southeast of Fort Gates, TX.
Large trees were knocked down in Turnersville in northern Coryell County. Minor damage was reported at the fire station.
Amateur radio reported power lines down near the Leon River Bridge.
Amateur radio reported a tree across the road and on a car.
Amateur radio reported trees down in Oglesby.
A trained spotter reported golf ball sized hail in Gatesville.
Hail damage to vehicles was reported at the fire station in North Fort Cavazos (formerly Ft Hood).
Dime to penny sized hail reported in Copperas Cove.
Amateur radio reported downed trees and power poles between Osage and Oglesby. VFDs had to clear tree debris from roadways. Reports were also received of a damaged roof and carport in the Osage area.
A trained spotter reported ping pong ball size hail in and around Arnett, TX.
A trained spotter reported quarter to golf ball size hail just south of Gatesville.

A suspected microburst caused damage along West Legends Way on Fort Cavazos. A display helicopter was turned over, large tree limbs were broken, power poles were knocked down and a few street signs were bent. At the firing range to the north, metal stands were moved and outhouses…

Damage was reported to a property on Conder Road, approximately 8 miles southwest of Pidcoke. Large trees were uprooted, split, and damaged. Small outhouses were also overturned, and the skirting was removed off a manufactured home.
A steel frame gazebo was blown over and tossed 10 feet off FM 116 in Copperas Cove.
Amateur radio reported half dollar size hail at FM 116 and US 190 in Copperas Cove.
Park service employees reported 1.25 inch hail at High Chapparal Dr and Hillside St in Copperas Cove.
Golf ball to tennis ball size hail reported by Inks Lake State Park official in Copperas Cove at Hillside Dr and High Chapparal Drive.
US Air Force personnel reported 1.25 inch hail at Fort Cavazos.
Trained spotter reported 1.25 inch hail in Copperas Cove.
Park and Forest Service personnel reported a few baseball to grapefruit size hail stones in south Copperas Cove.
Media reported quarter sized hail in Flat, Texas on Highway 36.
The AWOS at Gatesville Municipal Airport (KGOP) measured a 61 mph (53 kt) wind gust.
